text: Tampa Bay includes several Aquatic Preserves managed by the Florida Department of Environmental Protection, including the Pinellas, Boca Ciega Bay, Terra Ceia and Cockroach Bay Aquatic Preserves. But the proposed T-RICH site is at least ten miles from any of them. The site is also not believed to be near any High Consequence Area (HCA). A major release of CO from 2 the site is not expected to reach any dense population areas, schools, hospitals, or essential infrastructure. One exception may be the Tampa Electric Bayside Power Plant not far to the northeast of the site. It is theoretically possible that a release of CO could disrupt power generation there and cause power outages 2 in the surrounding region. However, a large release of CO from the site’s storage tanks or processing 2 equipment will likely travel south of the site, away from the power plant, and into an unpopulated area of Tampa Bay due to the innovative use of walls to direct released CO south and away from existing 2 adjacent industrial sites. This was analyzed in the CO dispersion analysis performed as part of the study 2 and discussed in the next section. The surrounding waterways comprising greater Tampa Bay may unofficially be considered environmentally sensitive areas even if they are not officially designated as such. Though it requires further study, it may be possible that a large release of CO into the bay south of the site may have a 2 detrimental effect on a very small number of birds and fish which might reside there or come to feed from time to time since it is a very remote location far from both port traffic and human interaction. But one of the major benefits of CO in this case is that, in the highly unlikely event of such a large spill, the escaped 2 CO will quickly warm up and evaporate before it reaches any designated ESAs or HCAs. And once it 2 evaporates soon after the spill, there is no longer any lingering potential for harm to the marine environment whatsoever. Accordingly, it is highly unlikely that any leakage will result in harm of loss of natural wildlife in the undeveloped aquatic area south of Pendola Point. It should be reiterated that the selection of this proposed site was based in large part on the existence of current adjacent industrial operations handling a range of products that are potentially harmful to the surrounding population and environment. Those include the liquefied petroleum gas storage and handling site directly to the east of this proposed site, and the ammonia storage, liquefaction and handling facility just to the north of the site. Both operations were evaluated in the past for their potential impact on the surrounding community and environment and found to be safe and appropriate for their location.
